Michael / Monica — draft technical bullets below for annex; keep it vendor-neutral and action-oriented so procurement/eng can review quickly. Feel free to paste into the Annex PDF.

- Recommended quantization path: start with calibrated int8 (post-training quantization) for the primary decoder model. Expected token-cost reduction: ~30–45% vs FP16 for typical conversational load.
- Aggressive option: mixed-int4 on non-critical endpoints (saves ~55–65%) but requires additional evals for hallucination/accuracy; recommend gating behind A/B test and quality monitors.
- Quality caveats: int4 may increase subtle generation variance on long-context prompts; plan for a 10–15% uplift in prompt-based evaluation checks during pilot.
- Fallback policy: automatic routing to FP16 or int8 sibling model when per-request quality signals (confidence thresholds or user-reported regressions) cross thresholds. Implement 2-minute failback cooldown to prevent oscillation.
- KV-cache sizing: for median prompt 60 tokens and 80 reqs/s peak, reserve ~4–8 GB cache per 100 concurrent KV sessions depending on model size; autosize policy: grow cache by 10% when cache hit rate < 40% and drop by 5% when hit rate > 80%.
- Operational notes: enable prefix caching on routes where prompt overlap >20% (observed in your demo traces) and add a token-level billing cap to the pilot proposal to limit tail cost exposure.

I'll add 1–2 references to measured savings from our internal benchmarks in the annex.

— Karthik
